sessions.phase_label: CRM architecture, tooling, and milestone planning
Integration testing, troubleshooting, and campaign launch

requirements.title: HubSpot CRM Configuration
requirements.definition: Configure HubSpot as the project's CRM using a plan that supports the accepted CRM workflows.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the HubSpot platform setup and selected tier, not the independently testable lead-transfer, campaign-synchronization, lead-management, or reporting behaviors.

requirements.title: Apollo Platform Configuration
requirements.definition: Configure Apollo, including the required plan and browser extension, for lead transfer and enrichment workflows.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers Apollo account and extension configuration; enrichment outcomes and cross-platform lead movement remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: MeetAlfred Platform Configuration
requirements.definition: Configure MeetAlfred on a plan that supports the required campaign integrations.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers platform setup and plan selection only; LinkedIn campaigns, email campaigns, campaign creation, and lead synchronization can change independently.

requirements.title: Zapier Platform Configuration
requirements.definition: Create and configure Zapier with the plan needed to operate the project's integrations.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers Zapier account, plan, and general configuration; each Zap-mediated business flow remains an independent Requirement.

requirements.title: LinkedIn-to-HubSpot Lead Transfer
requirements.definition: Move selected LinkedIn or Sales Navigator leads into HubSpot, using an accepted direct or Apollo-mediated workflow.
requirements.boundary_note: Direct Sales Navigator integration and the later Apollo-mediated process are alternative methods for the same lead-transfer behavior, not separate Requirements. Email enrichment and MeetAlfred delivery are independently testable.

requirements.title: Apollo Contact Enrichment
requirements.definition: Enrich lead records in Apollo with available email data and handle contacts for which no email can be found.
requirements.boundary_note: Enrichment success can be evaluated independently from transporting records between platforms; manual handling of unenriched contacts is part of this enrichment mechanism.

requirements.title: HubSpot-to-MeetAlfred Lead Synchronization
requirements.definition: Push qualifying leads from a HubSpot list through Zapier into the selected MeetAlfred campaign.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers lead synchronization into an already selected campaign. Creating a new MeetAlfred campaign and synchronizing activity status back to HubSpot are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: CRM Duplicate Visibility
requirements.definition: Make it possible to identify that a LinkedIn prospect already exists in the CRM before creating a duplicate record.
requirements.boundary_note: Duplicate visibility has its own expected decision outcome and is not merely an attribute of transporting leads into HubSpot.

requirements.title: LinkedIn Profile URL in CRM
requirements.definition: Store a normal LinkedIn profile URL in HubSpot rather than only a Sales Navigator-specific link.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently assessable field-mapping requirement and does not own the broader lead-transfer workflow.

requirements.title: Automated LinkedIn Campaigns
requirements.definition: Configure automated LinkedIn campaign execution in MeetAlfred.
requirements.boundary_note: LinkedIn campaign automation can be enabled, changed, or evaluated independently from email campaign automation and lead synchronization.

requirements.title: Automated Email Campaigns
requirements.definition: Configure automated email campaign execution in MeetAlfred.
requirements.boundary_note: Email campaign automation has a distinct delivery channel and can change independently from LinkedIn campaign automation.

requirements.title: Silent-Lead Follow-Up Automation
requirements.definition: Move silent leads from earlier CRM segments into follow-up campaigns without manually cleaning the earlier MeetAlfred campaigns.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a distinct recirculation workflow for silent leads rather than a generic campaign or list-sync attribute.

requirements.title: New MeetAlfred Campaign Workflow
requirements.definition: Provide a repeatable process for creating a new MeetAlfred campaign and configuring a corresponding Zap for HubSpot leads.
requirements.boundary_note: Campaign provisioning is independent from whether leads subsequently synchronize into the selected campaign.

requirements.title: Lead Communication History in HubSpot
requirements.definition: Expose each lead's relevant email and LinkedIn conversation history inside HubSpot.
requirements.boundary_note: Communication-history visibility is independently useful and testable, separate from lead status and general lead-management fields.

requirements.title: MeetAlfred Activity Status in HubSpot
requirements.definition: Update HubSpot's Lead Status field from MeetAlfred activity, including replies and accepted LinkedIn connections.
requirements.boundary_note: Status synchronization is a reverse activity flow with its own values and acceptance criteria, distinct from pushing HubSpot leads into MeetAlfred.

requirements.title: HubSpot Funnel Reporting
requirements.definition: Provide HubSpot reporting for the sales funnel, including grouping by Contact Source, stage breakdowns, and contact-to-lead conversion where supported.
requirements.boundary_note: The requested report dimensions are attributes of one funnel-reporting deliverable rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: CRM Data-Flow Map
requirements.definition: Produce a mapping of the data flow among the campaign platforms and HubSpot, including the MeetAlfred-to-HubSpot path.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently requested mapping artifact; it does not own the runtime state of the integrations it documents.

requirements.title: Campaign Domain Provisioning
requirements.definition: Select, purchase, and configure a separate campaign domain using the accepted registrar.
requirements.boundary_note: Domain acquisition and registrar configuration are separate from mailbox creation, forwarding behavior, and the one-off warm-up process.

requirements.title: Campaign Domain Forwarding
requirements.definition: Forward visitors from the campaign-domain address to the client's intended website destination.
requirements.boundary_note: The redirect is an independent runtime behavior and should not be merged into domain purchase or email warm-up.

requirements.title: Campaign-Domain Email Account
requirements.definition: Create and configure an email mailbox on the campaign domain using an accepted email provider.
requirements.boundary_note: Mailbox creation is independent from warming the mailbox and connecting it to campaign applications.

requirements.title: Campaign Domain and Mailbox Warm-Up
requirements.definition: Place the campaign domain and mailbox into an email warm-up process using the selected warm-up service.
requirements.boundary_note: Warm-up is a bounded operational task with its own defer/resume trajectory, distinct from the persistent mailbox and domain configurations.

requirements.title: Campaign Email Platform Integration
requirements.definition: Connect the campaign-domain email account with MeetAlfred and HubSpot before completing the deferred warm-up work.
requirements.boundary_note: Cross-platform mailbox integration is independently testable and should not be merged with mailbox creation or domain warm-up.

requirements.title: Timed Outbound Campaign Scripts
requirements.definition: Create outbound campaign scripts and multi-step sequences with defined timings for LinkedIn and email outreach.
requirements.boundary_note: Script content and timing are a distinct deliverable from executing campaigns, importing leads, or tracking them in the CRM.

requirements.title: Outbound Campaign Execution
requirements.definition: Run an outbound lead-generation campaign using an agreed mix of MeetAlfred automation and manual engagement.
requirements.boundary_note: The campaign objective is coherent, but the automation-versus-manual execution method remains unresolved and should be represented through later lifecycle evidence rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Outbound Lead Import and Tracking
requirements.definition: Track outbound leads and import them into the CRM so their progress can be managed after campaign activity.
requirements.boundary_note: Lead staging, import, and CRM tracking are independent from campaign execution and account concurrency.

requirements.title: Concurrent Outbound Accounts
requirements.definition: Support at least seven outbound accounts operating simultaneously.
requirements.boundary_note: The minimum simultaneous-account capacity is an independently testable scaling constraint; alias-versus-client account identity is an unresolved implementation choice.

requirements.title: HubSpot Lead Classification
requirements.definition: Provide HubSpot lead properties, tags, stages, categories, nurturing workflows, lists, notes, and task assignment needed to manage leads.
requirements.boundary_note: The listed properties, stages, tags, and task functions form one coupled lead-management mechanism; reporting and cross-platform status synchronization remain separate.

requirements.title: HubSpot Lead-Nurturing Workflows
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: HubSpot Lead-List Management
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: HubSpot Lead Notes
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: HubSpot Lead Task Assignment
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: MeetAlfred Integration Test-Data Safety
requirements.definition: Protect existing MeetAlfred campaigns and genuine leads during integration work by preserving active configurations and using mock or test leads.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a concrete data-preservation constraint on integration work, not a generic testing or QA Requirement.

requirements.title: MeetAlfred Integration Continuity
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: Obsolete Campaign Audience Message Suppression
requirements.definition: Prevent obsolete campaign audiences from receiving old messages and allow newly imported leads to be reviewed before further processing.
requirements.boundary_note: Audience activation and message-safety rules can change independently from the mechanics of importing leads.

requirements.title: New-Lead Review Before Processing
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client asks for email and LinkedIn chat history in HubSpot, but the supplied exchange does not clearly establish the exact supported sources, retention, or display behavior.
Domain forwarding is clearly requested, but the anonymized source and destination URLs appear identical, so the exact redirect mapping cannot be reconstructed safely.
Campaign-script creation is discussed as a priced future service, but the visible history does not clearly show that this separate engagement was commissioned.
The client prefers MeetAlfred automation for the prospective outbound campaign, while the freelancer recommends manual execution; no final client-approved execution method is visible.
At least seven simultaneous accounts is explicit, but account ownership, alias policy, and other scope details are deferred to an external document whose contents are not supplied.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Caleb Hart,

After taking some time to consider whether I had any more questions, I realized that a few points still need clarification. I hope you’re well, and I’m sorry for the delayed reply.

The workflow concern is easiest to explain first. Consider this scenario: Segment Cedar and Segment Maple are created in the CRM and then uploaded to MeetAlfred. Later, when both contain silent leads, I move those leads into Segment Quartz for a follow-up campaign. How can that new list then be exported seamlessly to MeetAlfred without requiring me to clean the earlier two campaigns manually? More generally, is there a way to place silent leads into follow-up campaigns without manually doing it in MeetAlfred?

I also need clarity on how existing records are identified. For someone already in the CRM, do I find out only after pressing the 'Export' button and receiving a 'duplicate' alert in the CRM, or is that status shown directly on the person’s LinkedIn profile?

There is a separate question about links: if data goes from Sales Navigator to the CRM, are LinkedIn profile links included while Sales Navigator links are excluded, since those links differ?

Finally, what is included within the 'Lead Management System', and inside Hubspot, will each lead’s email and LinkedIn chat history be visible?

value_updates.existing_record_visibility: Provide visibility into whether a LinkedIn prospect already exists in the CRM.

source_message.text: Network growth is all that automated campaigns help with; generating appointments requires us to engage in manual conversations.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Will you handle imports, and how will we track all the leads in our CRM?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: My requirement is to keep at least 7 accounts working simultaneously. Please give me some time to prepare a document containing my vision and questions, which should help us understand the scope better.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Thank you for the reply; my answers are below:

1\. There are two ways to make this possible:

a. One approach is to use the free <http://Apollo.io|Apollo.io> Google chrome extension. To support this approach, we need to adjust the flowchart slightly. Rather than sending leads directly to Hubspot CRM, we will export them into <http://Apollo.io|Apollo.io>, enrich the data there, and then export it to Hubspot. Since LinkedIn will display leads saved in <http://Apollo.io|Apollo.io>, we can avoid adding them again.

b. Another approach is to take a Linkmatch subscription. It integrates LinkedIn with Hubspot so the person's profile clearly shows whether he is in CRM or not. If he's not in CRM, he can be added to CRM in 3 clicks.

How can I tell whether a person is already in the CRM: will their LinkedIn profile show it, or will I find out only after pressing the 'Export' button and receiving a 'duplicate' alert in CRM?

2\. Ans. Under the normal integration, Hubspot receives Sales Navigator Data and link. Enriching the data through <http://Apollo.io|Apollo.io> or LinkMatch instead gives us a normail linkedIn URL.

When data is exported from Sales Navigator to the CRM, do I receive LinkedIn profile links rather than Sales Navigator links, since they are different?

3\. Ans. This is a system in which I would create custom properties and Tags, establish the Lead nurturing system, define the stages of leads, and categorize them properly. It covers List creations for dead or any other leads, along with Notes and a Task assigning system.

What is covered by the 'Lead Management System'?

Ans. Zaps make this possible. Will email and LinkedIn chat history for leads be visible inside Hubspot?

How can silent leads be added to follow-up campaigns without manually doing it in MeetAlfred?

Ans. For this step, I still need to check Meet Alfred. However, CRM can make it possible; we need to create 12 workflows inside the CRM system for that.

To clarify, suppose List A and List B are created in the CRM and uploaded into MeetAlfred. After silent leads emerge in both, I move those leads into a new List C for a follow-up campaign. How can that new list be exported seamlessly to MeetAlfred without requiring me to manually clean the former two campaigns?
